# Azure Key Vault Provider

<!-- status autogenerated section -->
<!-- end autogenerated section -->

## Summary

This Provider component offers a secure way to reference secrets or sensitive information in collector configurations using [Azure Key Vault](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/products/key-vault). Use a placeholder in the format `${azurekeyvault:https://{vault-name}.vault.azure.net/secrets/{secret-name}[/{version}]}` within your configuration. The actual secrets will then be fetched dynamically from Azure Key Vault during collector initialization.

## How it works

- Use placeholders with the following pattern: `${azurekeyvault:https://{vault-name}.vault.azure.net/secrets/{secret-name}}`
- To fetch a specific version: `${azurekeyvault:https://{vault-name}.vault.azure.net/secrets/{secret-name}/{version}}`
- If your secret is a JSON string, extract a specific key: `${azurekeyvault:https://{vault-name}.vault.azure.net/secrets/{secret-name}#json-key}`
- You can specify a default value: `${azurekeyvault:https://{vault-name}.vault.azure.net/secrets/{secret-name}:-default_value}`
  - The default value is used when the secret URL is invalid or the JSON key is not found

An example collector configuration:

```yaml
receivers:
  otlp:
    protocols:
      grpc:
      http:

exporters:
  logging:
    loglevel: debug
  otlphttp:
    endpoint: "https://example.com/api/metrics"
    headers:
      X-API-Key: ${azurekeyvault:https://myvault.vault.azure.net/secrets/api-key}

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [logging, otlphttp]
    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [logging, otlphttp]
    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      exporters: [logging, otlphttp]
```

### Prerequisites

1. The provider uses [Azure Default Credential](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/developer/go/azure-sdk-authentication) for authentication, which supports multiple authentication methods:
   - Managed identity (recommended for production on Azure)
   - Environment variables (`AZURE_CLIENT_ID`, `AZURE_TENANT_ID`, `AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET`)
   - Azure CLI (`az login`)
   - Workload identity (for Kubernetes)
2. Ensure the identity has the `Key Vault Secrets User` role or equivalent permission to read secrets from the Key Vault.
3. Secrets must already exist in Azure Key Vault before referencing them in the collector configuration.
